units.author: sb_roadworks
units.text: Day two. Dip still flooded but down to one lane, with a pump going and a man watching the pump. The temporary lights at the junction are working for the first time in a fortnight, presumably because the power stayed on. They are of course stuck on red in my direction. Normal service resumed.

units.author: sb_bins
units.text: Keep her in and don't fret. My late wife's two cats would never go out after the clocks changed, not for anything, and they lived to nineteen and twenty. Cats know their own minds about the dark. A litter tray by the back door is cheaper than worrying. Bernard (Rope Walk)

units.title: The old chiller in the bin store on 8
units.author: dc_2_hassan
units.text: Some people have asked me about the old shop chiller in the bin store on 8. Yes, it is mine. It is the drinks chiller from before the shop refit. It has been unplugged since the spring; I pulled the plug out myself and taped it to the side. It is waiting for the council bulky collection, who say 'next month' every month. I am sorry nobody thought to mention it before. H

units.author: sb_bins
units.text: Collected at 06:40 this morning, which I watched from the window with my tea. The box was then returned to number 14 instead of number 12. I have returned it to myself. I note the council's catch-up notice yesterday said 'Rope Walk tomorrow', which for once was accurate, and I want that on the record too. Bernard (Rope Walk)

units.author: trades_holm_work
units.text: Saw used_to_cut's last post. Fair play to him. He messaged me back near the start, when I was touting for subcontract work on the Holm, and told me straight not to take it. Never said why and I never asked. I listened, which isn't like me. Hope he's well wherever he is.

units.author: sb_bins
units.text: On question 2. The Co-op's goodwill form is mentioned on page 4 of the council newsletter of the 22nd, under 'Sound Power works', which nobody at the council seems to have read either. The threshold is twelve hours in total. Three forty-minute cuts a night for eight nights comes to sixteen. Write it down and send it in. Bernard (Rope Walk)

units.author: dc_7_irena
units.text: Dear neighbours, I have read the notice. I do not prop the door on 7, and I do not believe anyone on our floor does. I close it each time with my hand, the way my husband showed me when we came in 1984, and each morning it is closed. I mention only that I still hear the steps in the daytime, and that the door has nothing to do with it. Irena, 7C

units.author: dc_7_irena
units.text: Dear Hassan, thank you for the bread, which came up in the lift at ten past six still warm, and for knocking softly. Dear Mr Pryce, I am glad the left lift is working. I walked down from 7 to the shop and back yesterday with the shopping trolley and it took me twenty minutes, which is not bad for 74. Irena, 7C

units.author: sb_mod
units.text: A housekeeping note. The member 'used_to_cut_for_grieve' has closed his account. His earlier posts remain, as they do for anyone who leaves, and his name now shows greyed out. Please don't speculate about why he has gone. People are entitled to stop posting without explaining themselves to a forum.

units.title: Gallery door
units.author: lh_lighttender_tamsin
units.text: I've started keeping the gallery door shut at night. For years I stood out there between sweeps, hands on the rail, watching the beam go out over the water and the cliff path and come back. Now I watch from inside the lantern room, through the glass, with the door latched. Partly the rain, partly that I'm older than I was, partly a reason I'd rather not put into words. The light goes out the same either way.

units.author: lh_callcentre_tamsin
units.text: Sensible. Our building has a smokers' balcony on the fourth floor, and since the caller who described the edge of her porch light last week, nobody on nights goes out there alone. We go in threes and complain about the hold music. Between calls: you write the way the sea sounds on the line when someone rings from the coast road.

units.author: lh_kennel_orrin
units.text: Shutting a door is allowed. I've started bringing the dogs' night walk in by an hour so we're back inside before the yard light timer clicks over, and nobody has called me superstitious, they've called me sensible, mainly because Duke does his business faster when it's not raining on him.

units.title: Slipway sightings: the tide on each night.
units.author: skeptic_ferrous
units.text: I've put the tide tables against each reported night. Gilliver, the 4th: high water 23:40, so the slip was covered almost to the top in fog, and the figure was 'where the water starts', near the top. Gilliver, the 7th: low water 22:15, slip dry to its end, thick fog. Lisle, the 10th: half tide, drizzle. If any of these was a person messing about, the 7th is by far the easiest night. That isn't an accusation. It's a tide table.

units.author: retired_teacher
units.text: While we wait for Mr Ledger's references, may I ask whether anyone has thought of sending the crew something? The Lisle Women's Institute sent parcels to the lighthouse men every winter until the light was automated: socks, fruit cake, a newspaper a week old. It seems a small thing to do for people working through this weather.

units.author: retired_teacher
units.text: Thank you, Mr Ferrous. This is the first sensible post on the subject in some weeks. I would add only that the night of the 7th was also the night of the half-term disco at the Gilliver hall, which finished at ten. I make no suggestion. I taught for 34 years and I simply know what a half-term disco produces.

units.author: ferry_engineer_seth
units.text: Follow-up for those who asked about the deck floods. We've now got four 200 W heads on the wheelhouse roof and two on the stern rail, all on the genset, so they don't care what the shore supply is doing. Skipper's happy. Fuel burn's up about four percent. Somebody in head office is going to ask me about that and I'm going to tell them about the forty seconds.

units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: School bus over the ridge again, fine, ten minutes late, nobody wet. The youngest has started counting lit windows on the way home and says every farm on the ridge has a lamp on in the front room now. I said it's because it's dark at four. She said 'yes, that's what I said'. I can't argue with seven.

units.author: ferry_mate_kerris
units.text: I'm not arguing either. I'll say it once more the way I've always said it. Taller than me, dark coat, no light, standing at the end of the Gilliver slip where the water starts, two hails on the loud-hailer, no answer. I'm five foot ten. It was taller. Ada saw what she saw at Lisle. We don't have to have seen the same thing.

units.author: propwatch_ledger
units.text: Findings, with references as requested. 1. Besides the Holm, Ardent Vale Holdings holds four further properties through the same intermediary, Pellam Nominees. 2. Skellan Rock, a former radar station on an outer island, acquired fourteen months ago (ref PN/0219). 3. Hask Quarry, a worked-out quarry with no public road, acquired a year ago (ref PN/0233). 4. Tarrow Fort, a sea fort, 3.1 hectares (ref PN/0240). These were sent to me by a correspondent who works at a law firm.

units.author: propwatch_ledger
units.text: Findings continued. 5. Lyme Dale, an inland valley estate with a single private access track, acquired two years ago (ref PN/0187). 6. Tarrow Fort again, under a second reference (PN/0241), recorded as 31 hectares, which may be the foreshore included. All five sites are remote, and all were acquired within a short period. I have checked what I could. I would welcome corrections, and I mean that.

units.author: truthwatch_gil
units.text: There it is. A network. A radar station, a sea fort, a quarry with no road, a valley you can only reach by one track, and an island stripped bare so you can see across it. All remote, all bought at once, all through the same front company. Refuges. I said it on the 18th and got laughed at. Sending this to my list tonight, all 340 of you, share it.

units.author: gilliver_lamp
units.text: I dont understand any of the property talk and I wont pretend to. I only wanted to say the lights on the island came on early this afternoon in the rain, before four, because it gets dark so soon now. My lamp went on at the same time. I like to think of them seeing mine, though I know it is much too far.

units.title: Found: one small red mitten, Gilliver front
units.author: gilliver_lamp
units.text: Found on my front wall this afternoon, one small red knitted mitten with a white snowflake on the back, very wet. I have dried it on the rayburn and it is on my windowsill next to the lamp, so whoever lost it will see it from the road. It is a good mitten and somebody's grandmother made it. Maud, the house with the blue door.

units.title: What's everyone eating on break?
units.author: lh_student_kestrel
units.text: Survey, for science. What is everyone eating on break tonight? Me: cold noodles from 24h_counter_taro's shop, two energy drinks (I know, I know), and one satsuma for my conscience. Thesis chapter 4 is going about as well as the satsuma, which is to say it's in pieces on my desk and slightly sticky.

units.author: lh_convenience_kestrel
units.text: She bought the last satsuma. A man came in ten minutes later and asked for satsumas. I told him a student needed it more. He thought about this and accepted it. Then he bought nine energy drinks. Everyone is writing a thesis.

units.title: Available from next week: plant and chainsaw work
units.author: trades_holm_work
units.text: Hedge job in tollinby finishes friday so I'm free from next week. 3 tonne digger with driver, chainsaw tickets CS30 and CS31, chipper, trailer. Fencing, clearance, storm damage, fallen trees off drives. No job too small. Reasonable rates, no call-out fee within ten miles of port ammet. Not islands. Message me here.

units.title: Photo from the 17:50: settle an argument?
units.author: sb_commuter_lisle
units.text: Taken from the starboard rail of the 17:50 out of Port Ammet, around half six, as we came round toward Gilliver. Rain on the lens, sorry. In the middle there's a long pale bank of what looks like stacked timber, rows of it, cut ends towards the camera, with a single yellow lamp above it and something like a gate post at one end. Dark on both sides. My wife says it's the Holm through the zoom. I say it's the pallet stacks behind the Gilliver fish market. Who's right?

units.title: Last evening at the pier
units.author: lisle_crew_ada
units.text: Ha, so. Tonight's my last evening on the Lisle pier. I've taken a job at the surgery, days, on reception. Not because of any of this... mostly my back, and the bus, and my mum. The pier lights are the best they've ever been, which is typical. I'll miss the last ferry coming in round the point with everybody on deck in their coats. Be nice to whoever they get next.

units.author: harbour_admin
units.text: good luck ada. you were always the one on that pier who knew which lads had had a drink and got them off the boat without a fuss. take a coffee down to the new attendant on their first night and tell them where the switch for the pier lights is

units.author: skeptic_planner
units.text: Three problems before anyone shares this. 1. Lyme Dale is dated two years ago; Ardent Vale Holdings was incorporated eighteen months ago, according to its own filings. 2. Tarrow Fort appears twice, with two references and areas of 3.1 and 31 hectares. 3. Skellan Rock was sold at auction last spring to a seabird trust; it's in the trust's annual report, with photographs of the volunteers. And I can't find any 'PN' reference format on the registry at all.

units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: That's not the fish market. The pallets there are blue plastic and stacked flat, and there's nothing that size on Gilliver quay this month, I walk past it twice a day. Couldn't tell you what it is from a phone picture in rain. Could be anywhere along the shore with a lamp on it.

units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Lights out there were on from four. Supply boat went out at noon and came back sitting high, so she'd unloaded. Rain never stopped. Whatever anyone thinks about the company, them out there are working, and that's all I know about it, aye.

units.title: Gilliver feeder
units.author: lineman_garvey
units.text: Feeder's back and it's staying back. The insulator strings on the exposed spans are done, the last of them this afternoon in the flaming rain. Supply's been on since the small hours. That's all I'm saying on here, by request, so don't ask me anything else, lads.

units.author: trades_holm_work
units.text: Cut ends facing you, stacked in rows, one lamp over the top and a gate: that's a log yard mate, I've stood in a dozen of them. You stack by length and put the light where the loader turns. Where that one is I couldn't tell you, there's timber yards all down this coast.

units.author: harbour_admin
units.text: cheers garvey, nobody's asking, have a pint on me at the anchor. form went in this morning with everyone's times on it. bait freezer says thank you

units.author: wx_carrowpoint
units.text: Some numbers. At half six this evening the visibility in rain at my station was about 2,500 metres. The Holm is 9 km from Gilliver and further still from the ferry track. Whatever is in that photo is within two or three kilometres of the boat. I'd rule out the Holm on visibility alone, wife or no wife.

units.author: hobby_hydrophone
units.text: Answering Hollis. Boats on shore power that night: two. One small cruiser running a 12 V coolbox, which wouldn't give you mains hum. The other the Marigold, with a domestic fridge in the wheelhouse. She's been laid up since summer. I asked the owner. He says the fridge was off. Of course he does.

units.title: Something nice, please
units.author: dellow_admin
units.text: After a month of stairwells, doors, relays and chillers, could we have one thread for something nice? Anything. A good meal, a kind neighbour, a view from your window. I'll start. The print shop let me take home a box of misprinted calendars, and every month has the wrong picture on it. November is a beach. I now prefer it. Bev, DCRA

units.author: tern_audio
units.text: update. went up at seven this morning with the keeper and walked out to position two. nothing there, no kit, no bag, no tripod marks even, the rain had seen to that. and the car was gone from the car park. keeper says it went sometime in the night. I don't know if that's good. I think it's good.

units.title: Downpipe study: rain in a cast-iron gutter
units.author: hobby_hydrophone
units.text: Did the only sensible thing in this weather: hydrophone in the water butt under the old cast-iron downpipe at the back of the house. Every drip from the gutter arrives as a short knock, then the ring of the iron, then a gurgle in the butt. Some of you will find the knocks familiar. They are rain. Raw file, forty minutes, no edits.

units.author: dellow_admin
units.text: Please, let's not start interrogating the caretaker. He covers two buildings, he has one bad knee, and he's been asked about chairs by four different people this week. If he moved it, he moved it. Ivy, your drawing of him is lovely, and he's seen it, and he laughed. Bev, DCRA

units.author: sb_mod
units.text: This thread has become two different arguments, one about the crew and one about the company's other property, and neither is being served well by the other. I am locking part 3 and opening two new threads: 'Kittering Holm: the clearance and the crew.' and 'Ardent Vale's other properties (sources please).' Please continue there. And please read Planning Watcher's reply before sharing that list anywhere else.

units.title: Kittering Holm: the clearance and the crew.
units.author: sb_mod
units.text: This thread is for the clearance itself: the weather, the boats, the lights, and the people working on the island. Questions about the owner's other holdings belong in the other thread. Kindness is required here. Some of the crew's families read this board, and I would like them to find something here they're glad to have read.

units.title: Ardent Vale's other properties (sources please).
units.author: sb_mod
units.text: The rule for this thread: every claim needs a reference that somebody else can check. Mr Ledger's list is in the locked thread for anyone who wants to read it. I've quoted Planning Watcher's objections here so they sit at the top, where they belong. Rumours repeated without a source will be removed, whichever side they favour.

units.author: skeptic_hollis

edit.text: There it is: a compressor on floor 8, in the room next to where the recording was made, which is what I said on day 6. Edit: I've now read Hassan's post properly. Unplugged since spring, plug taped to the side. An unplugged compressor makes no noise at all. So it's the right machine in the right place, switched off. I'm not sure that settles anything, and I shouldn't have claimed it did.

units.text: There it is: a compressor on floor 8, in the room next to where the recording was made. I said on day 6 that the sound was a compressor, and here is the compressor. A drinks chiller cycles on its thermostat, carries through the slab, and sounds exactly like a slow tread in a concrete stairwell. I think we can call the fridge argument settled.

units.author: brackwater_keeper
units.text: Car went sometime between my last round at eleven and six this morning. Gate log has a vehicle out at 05:20, nobody in. Estate office says that's the end of it as far as they're concerned. A man's collected his own car with his own key. Leave it there, and stay out of my woods at night, the lot of you.

units.author: lineman_tess
units.text: Last post about work from me for a while. I've asked to move to day work and they've said yes, from next month. It's not because of anything on the line; there was never anything on the line, I walked every span of it. I just want to see what I'm fixing for a bit. Thanks to everyone who read the patrol notes, and to Garvey for teaching me all of it.

units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: My eldest's class are making cards 'for the tree people' because their teacher mentioned the island in geography and it got out of hand in the best way. There are glitter trees. Is there an address anyone knows? Or is that daft? I'd like to tell her something either way.

units.author: skeptic_hollis
units.text: Car collected at 05:20 by somebody with the key. That's the most ordinary fact in this whole thread. I'd now assume he's fine and embarrassed about something, which is what people usually are when they go quiet for two days. Tern, you did the right thing going up in daylight with the keeper.

units.author: skeptic_hollis
units.text: Lovely file. The ring of the pipe sits around 1.2 kHz. Pitch that down and slow it and you get something that sounds uncannily like a word, which is how a few 'voices' have come about over the years. Not a dig at anyone. It's just useful to have a clean reference of rain on iron.

units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Lights on along the front all evening and steady with it. First time in a week I've walked up the hill without a torch in my pocket. My aunt says to tell the linemen thank you, and to tell the young lass she'll do well on days.

units.author: dc_2_hassan
units.text: Something nice: the new bakery supplier does a seeded loaf that sells out every morning by eight. People queue for it now, in the rain, and talk to each other in the queue. I keep one back every day for 7C. Also the cat from 4 has started sleeping on the newspapers. I let her. H

units.author: wx_carrowpoint
units.text: Station summary, for the record. 22 mm today, wind SE 4, no fog at any point, nothing on the salt plate again. My power logger shows no interruptions since 01:48 last night, which is the longest unbroken run since the cuts began. Long may it last.

units.author: tern_audio
units.text: ok so. if he collected his car he could have texted. one text. sorry, that's mean. I'm glad. I'm also annoyed. both at once, which my mum says is what caring about people is mostly like.

units.author: hobby_binaural
units.text: Headphones on, tea made, relief. Tern, annoyed is allowed. You walked out to the outflow in the rain for him. When he turns up, he owes you a pint and an explanation, in that order, and you can have the pint even if you don't get the explanation.

units.author: truthwatch_gil
units.text: Planning Watcher's points are nitpicks. A typo in an area figure doesn't make a fort disappear. A wrong date doesn't make a valley disappear. The registry wouldn't use the same reference format as a nominee company's internal files anyway, that's the whole point of nominees. It's already gone out to my list and people are thanking me.

units.author: hobby_binaural
units.text: Headphones on for the downpipe. It's oddly lovely: the knock is left and low, the ring spreads out above it, and the gurgle stays put. A binaural version from inside a water butt would be very wet and very short-lived, so I'll leave this one to you.

units.author: lowband_mod
units.text: Thanks, everyone. I'm going to leave this thread open but quiet. If anyone hears from him directly, a one-line 'he's fine' is plenty. Nobody owes us more than that, and I'd like to keep it that way for anyone who goes quiet in future, including me.

units.author: skeptic_brisk
units.text: A radar station, a fort and a quarry. Lads. It's a rich bloke who likes buying old military junk. My uncle bought a tank once. It's in a barn in Tollinby with chickens living in it. Nobody's hiding from anything in my uncle's tank.

units.author: dc_8_benedikt
units.text: I did not know this chiller. I said there was no fridge on that floor. I was wrong about this, sorry. But Hassan says unplugged. I still have a key for the bin store from when I carried bags for Irena. Tomorrow after my shift I will go and check myself and write what I see.

units.author: gilliver_teen
units.text: Okay. I need to say this properly and without being an idiot for once. On the night of the 7th, in the fog, after the hall disco, I stood at the end of the Gilliver slipway in my grandad's long waxed coat for about ten minutes because people dared me to. The late ferry went past. Nobody hailed me. I came home and said nothing. I'm sorry. That's one night. I wasn't there on the 4th. I've never been to Lisle at night. I only did it once.

units.author: dc_6_jordie
units.text: something nice: passed my circuits exam. 71. the cardio of doom made me fit enough to sit in an exam hall for three hours without fainting, so in a way the stairwell deserves some credit. also irena gave me a slice of honey cake for carrying her shopping and it was the best thing I've eaten this year

units.author: skeptic_brisk
units.text: Told you. Told every single one of you, weeks ago. A kid in a coat. Weeks of this, newspaper pieces, 'crew welfare reviews', and it was a kid in his grandad's coat. Lads, I said it was a kid. I'd like an apology from the whole board, in alphabetical order.

units.author: truthwatch_gil
units.text: Convenient timing for a confession, the very evening a property list comes out that someone doesn't want people talking about. Just asking: who asked him to post this tonight? Why now, after three weeks? I'm not saying he's lying. I'm saying ask.

units.author: skeptic_brisk
units.text: Nobody asked him, Gil. He's seventeen, it's Gilliver, his mum found out. That's the whole conspiracy. You've been wrong about everything for a month and I've been right about one thing and I intend to enjoy it.

units.author: lh_crane_halvard
units.text: Night two of keeping it simple. Rain in the cab tonight, coming in round the door seal and dripping on my left boot. One lift of formwork, one of a portable toilet, which is the most dignified thing I've ever flown. No questions. Okay, one: does anyone else's flask lid leak, or have I been sold a lemon for three years?

units.title: Front door intercom
units.author: lh_carer_vellmark
units.text: A short one, and I'm sorry if it's sad. Since Mrs A. died last week, very peacefully, with her daughter holding her hand, the front door intercom has been quiet. No buzz at 03:10. The electrician dried out the junction box weeks ago and it should have stopped then, and it didn't. Now it has. I don't know what I think about that. I'm writing it down because she'd have liked someone to.

units.author: morrow_unknown
units.text: Not daft at all, I don't think. I don't know an address, sorry. I'd guess the company would pass things on if someone asked them politely. The lights on the island were on tonight in the rain, two of them, same as last night. I might be wrong but glitter trees seem like exactly the right thing.

units.title: Floor 10 and up: does anyone run in the mornings?
units.author: dc_6_jordie
units.text: ok hear me out. what if the cardio of doom is literally cardio. somebody on 10 or above with a treadmill, footsteps carrying down the riser wall, the structure-borne thing hollis keeps saying. I'm only about 40 percent joking. does anyone in the building own a treadmill. asking for the stairwell.

units.author: lh_baker_coriveth
units.text: Burnt ends of the rye, still warm, with salted butter, eaten standing at the back door watching the rain come down the alley in a little river. Ten out of ten. Satsuma solidarity from the harbour, though; we all need one thing on the plate that makes us feel like a responsible adult.

units.author: dc_9_tobin
units.text: Observations. 1. Running on a treadmill produces roughly 150 to 170 impacts per minute. 2. Benedikt's recording shows about 100 per minute, which is consistent with someone descending stairs at an ordinary pace. 3. Walking on a treadmill would be closer. 4. I am not counting. I am reading a number I already had.

units.author: lh_dockguard_coriveth
units.text: 03:20 one baker's roll, one flask of lentil soup, one apple, eaten in the gatehouse watching camera 3. The fox did not appear. I note this without concern. Nil found. Satsuma noted for future logs.

units.author: hollow_signal
units.text: Four places with nothing around them. The Holm is the fifth... Some of us have understood the shape of this for a long time. A fort, a rock, a quarry, a valley. Places you can see coming. The details don't matter. The pattern does. I've said more than I should.

units.author: dc_14_ivy
units.text: Something nice: from 14 at sunset, in the half hour before the rain came back, the whole dock went gold and the cranes looked like (very tall, very patient) herons standing in a pond. I drew them. Six herons. I've pinned the drawing up in the left lift, which is working, which is also nice.

units.author: lh_nurse_halvard
units.text: Ours said one more name last week, a different one, and then nothing since. I'm not reading into mine, and you don't have to read into yours. What I will say is that she was lucky in the people who looked after her at night. Thinking of you, and of her. Back to it.

units.author: morrow_unknown
units.text: I might be wrong, and I'm not good with registries. But the list doesn't feel right to me. If someone really were buying places to hide in, why would the details turn up through a correspondent at a law firm, with two different sizes for the same fort? It reads more like something put together than something found. Sorry.

units.author: lh_security_st
units.text: Control brought a cake into the gatehouse for someone's birthday and left it on the desk with a knife in it. It isn't anyone's birthday. Nobody can work out whose it was meant to be. We're eating it anyway, a slice per patrol, which has done wonders for patrol numbers.

units.author: skeptic_dmitra
units.text: Shutting a door against rain at two in the morning isn't a symptom of anything. It's a good idea, and an old one. If you ever notice the reason changing from the weather to something else, that's when I'd say sleep more and talk to someone. Until then: dry feet, warm tea, glass between you and the weather.

units.author: lh_mod
units.text: Housekeeping: this is a lovely thread and I'm leaving it be. A gentle reminder that anything about 'standing at the edge of the light' goes in the merged thread from last week, not here. Lamp and lens, keep the door shut and the kettle on.

units.author: lh_porter_portammet
units.text: Orange crisps. Obviously. They are now the only crisps, by order of the vending machine, and I have come to love them the way you love a difficult relative. Also half a sausage roll that the night sister declared 'surplus to requirements'. Back on the run.

units.author: lh_taxi_halvard
units.text: my flask lid leaks bo, it's leaked since 2009, it's a feature, you learn to drink from the side that doesn't drip anyway the rank was dead tonight so I sat under the hospital lamp with the engine off and listened to the rain on the roof for an hour and got paid nothing for it and enjoyed it

units.author: lh_picker_weyhaven
units.text: protein bar that tastes of a gym bag and a coffee from the machine that has been 'temporarily' out of milk since the spring. the target tonight is 180 an hour, I'm at 162, the satsuma would not help. break's eleven minutes and I've used nine of them writing this

units.author: lh_insomniac_tollinby
units.text: It took some courage to post that under your own name, at your age, on a board where you know the regulars will be unkind. I hope the people who were frightened by that night accept the apology, in time. Most of the good characters in the books I sell get one big thing wrong and then own it.

units.author: lh_insomniac_tollinby
units.text: Not daft. If the cards go, I've a box of old paperbacks I'd happily put in with them: thick ones, mysteries mostly, with nothing sad in them. Nights out there must be long, and there's a particular comfort in a book somebody else has already folded the corners of.

units.author: lh_miner_vellmark
units.text: Proud of you, Liv. On the bus now. Thirty years underground and I've never seen anyone sit with the old ones like you do. Intercom or no intercom. Home in twenty. Kettle on.

units.title: A month of 'edge of the light': where we are
units.author: skeptic_orla
units.text: I'll say it here because the merged thread has got long. Listener stories travel. I've heard the 'someone standing just past the light' story arrive on my show from three different towns in nearly the same words, each caller sure it was their own. That doesn't make anybody a liar. It makes them listeners. I'm still not buying it, and I don't think a month of it changes that.

units.author: lh_miner_vellmark
units.text: Old men at the pit say you stay inside the lamp. Your gallery door is the same rule, by the sound of it. Tradition, not belief, is what I always say. Good rule either way. Keeps your boots dry and your head clear.

units.author: skeptic_dmitra
units.text: Agree. The one thing I'd add after a month of reading every report: they cluster where people are tired, alone and looking at the line between lit and unlit ground. That boundary is exactly where human vision is at its worst, and where the brain fills in the most. It doesn't need anything else to explain it. That isn't the same as saying nobody saw anything.

units.author: hollow_signal
units.text: Or the reports cluster where they are... Tired people at the edge of the light are the only ones still looking. Everyone else is asleep. Think about that before you explain it away again.

units.author: dc_10_garrick
units.text: Morning legends. Yeah mate, that's me. Treadmill in the back bedroom on 10, been there two years, heavy commercial unit I got off the gym when they refitted. I'm on it most mornings before clients, walking warm-up then a run. Never thought about it carrying through the riser, but that bedroom wall backs straight onto it. Sorry if it's been me all this time. Happy to put a proper mat under it.

units.author: dc_5_lorna
units.text: well that's a lovely thought love and I'd be ever so pleased if it was you, a nice young man running about on 10 with his music on, I come in at five most days and I've never heard a treadmill mind you, but then I've never heard anything at all on those stairs which is what I always say
